label: US Unemployment Rate
deltaNote: June 2026 (July 2): Unemployment fell to 4.2% (vs 4.3% expected) — but largely because labor-force participation dropped to 61.5%, the lowest since March 2021, rather than from underlying strength. June NFP +57,000, a sharp slowdown from May's downwardly-revised +129,000; April/May combined revised down 74,000. Average hourly earnings +0.3% to $37.64 (+3.5% YoY).

label: US PCE Inflation (May 2026 — Highest Since 2023)
deltaNote: MAY 2026 (released June 25): Headline PCE 4.1% YoY (+0.4% MoM) — highest since April 2023. Core PCE 3.4% YoY (vs 3.3% forecast). Personal income and spending each +0.7% MoM; saving rate held at 3%. Released just over a week after Warsh's hawkish dot plot, complicating the disinflation narrative even as Iran-deal oil relief began working through the data. June CPI (July 14) subsequently cooled to 3.5%, suggesting May PCE may mark the cycle high.

label: Fed Funds Rate

delta: Held; hawkish dot plot signals hike ahead
deltaNote: June 16-17: Warsh's first FOMC as Chair unanimously held at 3.50-3.75%. The Summary of Economic Projections turned hawkish: 2026 median dot rose to 3.8% from 3.4% in March — implying a hike, not a cut — with 9 of 18 members projecting ≥1 hike. 2026 PCE forecast raised to 3.6% from 2.7%. Warsh declined to submit his own dot. Next FOMC July 28-29 is a non-SEP meeting; consensus expects another hold.

label: ECB Deposit Facility Rate

deltaNote: June 11: ECB raised all three key rates 25bp — deposit facility to 2.25%, main refi to 2.40%, marginal lending to 2.65% (effective June 17). First hike since July 2023, reversing the final step of the prior 8-cut easing cycle. New staff projections: HICP 3.0% (2026)/2.3% (2027)/2.0% (2028); growth cut to 0.8%/1.2%/1.5%. Lagarde left the door open to further tightening.

label: Michigan Consumer Sentiment (May 2026 Final)
deltaNote: MAY 2026 FINAL — THIRD CONSECUTIVE ALL-TIME RECORD LOW: 44.8 shatters April's 47.6 record (already below 1980 energy crisis nadir of 51.7). Preliminary reading was 48.2; final collapsed 3.4 points — unusually large revision. Year-ahead inflation expectations: 4.5% (down from April's 4.7% — the largest one-month jump in survey history). ~1/3 of respondents spontaneously mentioned gasoline prices; ~30% mentioned tariffs. Deepest consumer pessimism in the survey's 70+ year history. S&P 500 closed 8 consecutive weekly gains (7,473.47); the sentiment/spending divergence has never been wider.

label: S&P 500 / Market Risk Gauge

delta: Markets round-tripped the June scare: after the June 5 -2.6% drop, the signed Iran MOU (June 17) and subsequent oil-price collapse drove a relief rally into H1 close (S&P +9.6%, 24 record closes). June's weak jobs report (July 2) and cooling June CPI (July 14, 3.5%) both supported further gains — S&P closed July 14 at 7,572.40 (+0.38%), Nasdaq +0.62% to 26,269.23, Dow +150 pts to 52,658.64.
deltaNote: JUNE-JULY ARC: Triple central bank week (ECB hike Jun 11, BOJ hike Jun 16, Warsh hawkish dot plot Jun 17) was more than offset by the same-day signed Iran MOU, which crashed Brent ~11% and triggered a broad risk-on rally. Goldman confirmed its 15% 12-month US recession probability on June 22 post-deal. H1 2026 closed +9.6% for the S&P (best first half since 2020) and +12.8% for Nasdaq, with the Russell 2000 up ~22% (best since 1991). Weak June jobs (NFP +57K, Jul 2) and cooling June CPI (3.5%, Jul 14) reinforced a 'goldilocks' market read heading into the July 24 Section 122 tariff cliff and July 28-29 FOMC.

label: US Avg Effective Tariff Rate
value: 8.9% overall; ~31.6% China effective; Section 122 Cliff July 24 — 8 Days Away; Section 301 Fallback Timing in Doubt
source: Penn Wharton / CBP / USTR Greer CBS Face the Nation / Gibson Dunn / BDO, May 17 2026
contestNote: Section 122 baseline unchanged at 8.9% overall / 31.6% China effective. Federal Circuit stay (June 11) keeps Section 122 tariffs collected pending appeal, but the underlying July 24 statutory cliff is unaffected by the stay. USTR's Section 301 fallback (60 economies, forced-labor rationale) closed its comment period July 6 and held its hearing July 7 — but standard rulemaking requires a final rule ≥30 days before taking effect, meaning Section 301 may not be ready to fully backstop the cliff, raising the prospect of a tariff-revenue coverage gap. No Congressional action to extend Section 122 has been reported; an extension needs 60 Senate votes.

label: BOJ Policy Rate
source: Bank of Japan, June 16 2026 (25bp hike — highest since 1995)
deltaNote: June 16: BOJ hiked 25bp to 1.00%, the highest level since 1995, in a 7-1 vote (Asada dissenting) — citing Iran-war energy-cost pass-through risk. The hike landed the same day Warsh's first FOMC opened, raising August-2024-style carry-unwind concerns; the immediate market reaction was orderly (Nikkei +0.46%), but the yen still fell to a fresh 40-year low past 162/USD by June 30 despite the hike and an estimated $72.5bn in prior FX intervention.
